$doc: Hand-written, justified overrides for jury SPLIT verdicts (issue #20; gate_jury.py's docstring: "the item is investigated and either fixed, dropped, or explicitly adjudicated ... committed, hand-written, with justification"). Every entry here is a SPLIT (1-1 juror disagreement, no majority) — gate_jury.py's scoring never lets a REFUTED-MAJORITY item pass via adjudication, by design, so nothing below overrides a consensus finding. Re-run tools/gate_jury.py after editing this file so leg-jury.json's recorded `pass`/`adjudication` fields pick up the change.

adjudications.context:不|也|看: Juror self-contradiction, not a real disagreement: gpt-4.1-2025-04-14's own note concludes '...the rule name and surface are correct. No error.' while its verdict field says 'error' — the two are inconsistent within the same juror response. gpt-5.2-2025-12-11 independently confirms bu2 before kan4 (tone 4) is the correct tone-shift-before-4 surface. The reading is undisputed by both jurors' own reasoning; only one juror's verdict field mis-recorded its own conclusion.
adjudications.sentence:s15: Juror self-contradiction, not a real disagreement: gpt-4.1-2025-04-14's own note explicitly concludes '...No error here; this is acceptable. Correction: no-error.' while its verdict field says 'error' — the juror's verdict field contradicts its own stated correction. gpt-5.2-2025-12-11 independently verdicts no-error. 不 stays bu4 before 知道 (zhi1dao5, base tone 1) per the standard tone-shift-before-4 rule (no shift applies outside tone 4) — correctly pinned.
adjudications.sentence:s36: Documented neutral-register variation, not an error: gpt-5.2-2025-12-11 flags 學生 pinned as xue2 sheng5 (neutral tone) and expects xue2 sheng1 (full tone). This is exactly the neutral-register agreement class this curation gate's own tooling documents and expects (tools/gate_lib.py module docstring: '個 ge4/ge5, 學生 sheng5/sheng1, 朋友 you5/you3 class — dictionaries pin citation tones, Taiwan usage neutralizes some, tools differ by register'). gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 independently verdicts no-error. Both readings are attested; the sliver pins the Taiwan-colloquial neutral-tone register, consistent with every other neutral-tone word in the sliver (see words.json).
adjudications.sentence:s46: Documented neutral-register variation, not an error (same class as sentence:s36): gpt-5.2-2025-12-11 flags 喜歡 pinned as xi3 huan5 (neutral tone) and expects xi3 huan1 (full tone). words.json pins citationPinyin == surfacePinyin == ['xi3','huan5'] deliberately — the Taiwan-colloquial neutral-tone register for the second syllable, the same documented tools/gate_lib.py class ('個 ge4/ge5 ... 朋友 you5/you3 class'). gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 independently verdicts no-error.

Same class as the 嗎/的-carrier entries below — the carrier is a deliberately minimal single-context verification instrument (see gate_jury.py's context-item framing, added after this run to state that terseness alone is not a defect), not a display sentence.

adjudications.sentence:s05: Deliberate segmentation convention, not an error: gpt-5.2-2025-12-11 objects to 星期一 being cut as 星期|一 rather than one token. This sliver deliberately treats weekday numerals as compositional (星期 + the C3 single 一, so C9's ordinal-date context enumeration can pin 一's unshifted reading in this exact role) — the same convention already recorded in segmenter-normalization.json (jieba's natural 星期一 boundary is mapped back to the pinned 星期|一 cut) and now stated directly in the sentence-item prompt text (added after this run) alongside the other listed segmentation conventions. gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 independently verdicts no-error.

classNote: The 21 嗎|X|<END> and 的|X|Y entries above share one pattern: gpt-5.2-2025-12-11 flags the C9 carrier sentence as an unnaturally terse fragment in isolation (a bare 'X嗎？' question or a bare possessive+noun with no established referent), while gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 verdicts no-error on every one of them. In EVERY case both jurors' own notes agree the READING under test (嗎=ma5, 的=de5) is correct — the disagreement is purely about carrier-sentence naturalness, not about the pinned reading C9 exists to verify. This is expected and by design: build_assets.py auto-generates one minimal carrier sentence per enumerated (char, prev, next) context — see src/sidecars/zh/curation/tools/gate_sandhi.py's own module docstring, which independently classifies carriers as 'verification instruments, not display candidates' (point 3) — so a carrier reading tersely out of context is the intended shape, not a curation defect. None of these 21 sentences are ever shown to a learner; they exist solely to pin a (char, prev, next) -> reading mapping for #19's fail-closed context lookup.
